name: Mitochondrial Membrane Transport Disorder

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Mitochondrial Membrane Transport Disorder Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Identification of pathogenic variants in genes encoding mitochondrial membrane transport proteins
Demonstration of impaired mitochondrial membrane transport function via biochemical assays
Presence of multisystemic clinical manifestations consistent with mitochondrial dysfunction
Muscle biopsy showing mitochondrial abnormalities such as ragged-red fibers or abnormal cristae

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Pathogenic genetic variant identification plus biochemical evidence of mitochondrial membrane transport impairment
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis may be supported by clinical features and histopathology but requires genetic and biochemical confirmation.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Exercise intolerance due to impaired oxidative phosphorylation
searchTerms: exercise intolerance from poor energy production
fatigue during exercise due to oxidative phosphorylation defect
low exercise capacity from mitochondrial issues

common.notes: Elevated blood lactate levels due to mitochondrial dysfunction

searchTerms: weakness mainly in upper arms and thighs
muscle weakness close to body center
endocrine dysfunction with high blood sugar

rare.notes: Progressive degeneration of the optic nerve

laboratory: Elevated blood and CSF lactate and pyruvate
Abnormal mitochondrial respiratory chain enzyme activities
imaging: Brain MRI showing basal ganglia signal abnormalities
Muscle MRI demonstrating fatty infiltration and atrophy
genetic: Pathogenic variants in SLC25 family genes (e.g., SLC25A4, SLC25A20)
Mitochondrial DNA depletion or deletions associated with transport defects
other: Muscle biopsy with ragged-red fibers and abnormal mitochondrial ultrastructure

distinguishingFeatures: Marked mitochondrial DNA depletion on muscle biopsy
Absence of specific membrane transport protein mutations
Predominantly muscle involvement without transport protein defects
Variable genetic causes unrelated to membrane transport

redFlags: Rapidly progressive external ophthalmoplegia in childhood
Severe lactic acidosis refractory to treatment
Multisystemic involvement with cardiomyopathy and neuropathy
references: DiMauro S, Schon EA. Mitochondrial respiratory-chain diseases. N Engl J Med. 2003 Jun 19;348(26):2656-68.
Spinazzola A, Zeviani M. Disorders from defects of mitochondrial carriers: a review. Biochim Biophys Acta. 2009 May;1797(6-7):564-78.
